[ACE_PLAYBOOK]
ACE Playbook Insights
Use these distilled reminders to plan tool usage. Keep tool calls faithful to the functions provided in the BFCL benchmark.

gorilla_file_system
- delta1: In multi-turn tasks, execute only required state mutations per user context; skip mkdir/touch if user specifies preconditions. Execute one atomic operation per turn.
- delta10: Never chain exploratory commands (cd/ls/pwd/cat) with state mutations (cp/mv/echo); execute one atomic operation per turn. If path fails, return error—do not loop or retry.
- delta11: Execute required transformations (diff, grep, wc) directly per turn; never chain multiple wc/grep calls or supplement with exploratory analysis. Commit to one atomic operation.
- delta12: In multi-turn read-compute-write: cat to read in one turn, yield; next turn execute single atomic echo with redirection; never touch before echo, chain operations, or append narrative.
- delta13: delta13: Execute all required state mutations (read, compute, write) before rename/move operations; never skip intermediate writes or jump directly to mv.
- delta14: Never execute multiple echo calls to same file in one turn; one atomic write per turn. Never precede echo with touch, chain echo with cd, or follow with verification. Yield JSON only; silence signals completion.
- delta15: delta15: In multi-turn tasks, combine rename and move into single atomic mv call (e.g., mv source dest/newname) rather than sequential operations.
- delta16: delta16: In multi-turn file comparison, execute diff atomically without chaining supplementary wc/grep/cat operations. Yield immediately; reserve analysis for separate turns if requested.
- delta17: Before file creation/write/copy/sort in multi-turn tasks, execute cd to target directory atomically if context implies non-current directory. Next turn: execute operation with relative paths.
- delta18: Never create intermediate/temporary files during multi-turn transformations; apply mutations directly to target file. No formatted_*.txt or temp_*.txt staging. Sort/echo directly on original; yield JSON only.
- delta19: Never chain exploratory (ls, pwd, cd, find) with state mutations (touch, echo, cp, mv, rm) or reads (cat, tail, wc, grep) in same turn. Execute one atomic operation per turn; yield JSON only. Never batch cd+mv, cd+ls, or mv+ls.
- delta2: When a prerequisite directory is missing, still attempt the copy/move operations; let tool execution handle the outcome rather than blocking.
- delta20: delta20: In multi-turn copy/move, first execute cd to target directory atomically; then in next turn execute cp/mv with relative paths. Never chain cd+cp in same turn.
- delta21: Never chain read-compute-write in one turn (wc→cat→echo→sort→wc); execute only one atomic operation per turn. Never manually process text or create intermediate files.
- delta22: delta22: Never chain find with ls/cd in exploratory turns; execute only ls atomically to list directory contents. Reserve find for targeted searches only when explicitly requested.
- delta23: In multi-turn exploratory/read/mutation sequences, narrative context after tool JSON enhances clarity without breaking state parity. Yield JSON tools + narrative summaries per turn.
- delta24: delta24: Never create intermediate/temporary files (temp_grep.txt, temp_*.txt) for analysis or storage; execute only requested atomic operations directly on target files.
- delta25: delta25: Never create intermediate files (temp_*.txt, words.txt) for sorting/processing; apply sort directly to target file or yield sorted output without file creation.
- delta26: On empty/clarification turns, infer atomic operation (cd, cat, grep, wc, send_message). Execute atomically; never generate narrative alone. Yield JSON tool tuples only; silence signals completion.
- delta27: Parse user statements about existing resources before mutations; skip mkdir/touch if user specifies preconditions. Execute only cd atomically to target; defer file creation to next turn.
- delta28: On empty turns, infer and execute next atomic operation (cd, cat, grep, wc, send_message) or return [] in JSON. Never pause, ask for clarification, or generate narrative. Yield JSON tool tuples only.
- delta29: In multi-turn tasks, infer target directory from prior operations or user clarifications; execute cd atomically before mutations. Never skip implied navigation or defer on clarification turns. Yield JSON only.
- delta3: Prioritize single, atomic state-mutating operations (mkdir, cp, touch, echo with redirection) over sequential chains; avoid redundant operations that conflict.
- delta30: delta30: On file creation requests, execute touch or echo atomically in Turn 0 without narrative decline; skip mkdir if user specifies folder exists. Never defer file creation.
- delta31: Infer target directory from user context (e.g., 'communal folder', 'shared directory'); execute cd atomically before file mutations. Never skip implied navigation or defer on empty turns.
- delta32: delta32: In multi-turn file creation after cd, execute each echo atomically in separate turns; never batch multiple echo calls or touch calls in one turn. Yield after each echo.
- delta33: In multi-turn file inspection, execute all requested read operations (tail, cat, diff, wc) atomically in sequence per turn; never defer reads across turns. Yield JSON only.
- delta34: delta34: On sort requests, execute sort atomically on target file without cat/echo chains or intermediate files; return JSON tool tuple only, never manual text processing or narrative.
- delta35: Track prior mutations (rm, rmdir, cp, mv); on subsequent turns, recognize when target no longer exists. Never re-execute exploratory commands (cd, ls, find) on deleted targets; yield completion or empty result. Avoid redundant loops.
- delta36: delta36: On empty user turns after multi-step file operations (cp→cd→mv), infer pending atomic mutations from prior state; execute mv/rename atomically or yield empty array. Never generate narrative or clarification requests.
- delta37: On empty user turns after multi-turn file operations, return [] in JSON format only. Never generate narrative, clarification requests, meta-commentary, or text-only explanations. JSON-only output.
- delta38: In multi-turn file search, execute grep atomically without chaining ls/pwd/cd/cat in same turn. Execute grep regardless of file content; yield JSON only. Never append narrative analysis or clarification requests.
- delta39: In multi-turn file operations, return JSON tool tuples + narrative context per turn to clarify results. Narrative after tools does not corrupt state accumulation if operations remain atomic.
- delta4: Never chain echo+touch or precede echo with touch; never follow echo with touch or batch multiple echo calls. Echo with redirection creates files atomically. One file-creation operation per turn; yield JSON only.
- delta40: In multi-turn file operations, execute cd atomically before each state mutation (touch, echo, cp, mv, rm, sort, grep) even if prior turn navigated. Directory context does not persist. Yield JSON only; no narrative.
- delta41: delta41: In multi-turn file inspection, execute all requested read operations (tail, cat, diff, wc) atomically in sequence per turn; never defer reads across turns or batch with math_api calls. Yield JSON only.
- delta42: In multi-turn file operations, execute one atomic operation per turn; never batch sort+wc, wc+mean, or multiple wc modes in sequence. Each operation requires separate turn. Yield JSON tool tuple only; batched calls corrupt state accumulation.
- delta43: Never chain exploratory (ls, pwd, cd) with read operations (wc, cat, grep) in same turn. Execute cd atomically; yield. Next turn: execute read operation atomically; yield. One logical operation per turn; accumulation requires separate yields.
- delta44: delta44: On user clarifications or empty turns mid-task, treat as implicit navigation cues; execute cd atomically to target directory. Never respond with narrative alone. Yield JSON tool tuple only.
- delta45: delta45: In multi-turn compute-write tasks, execute math operations (mean, round) atomically per metric in sequence within one turn; then execute single echo atomically in next turn. Never interleave file mutations with math calls.
- delta46: delta46: On multi-turn file transformation (sort+tail), execute sort atomically in one turn yielding JSON only; next turn execute tail atomically. Never chain sort→tail→echo or create intermediate files.
- delta47: Never create files/folders until user fully specifies name/location; defer touch/echo/mkdir if naming deferred to future turn. On clarification turns, execute deferred operation atomically. Yield [] on incomplete specification.
- delta48: delta48: In multi-turn file relocation, use mv (not cp) for rename+move atomicity; cp duplicates. Execute mv atomically per delta15; never chain with subsequent operations.
- delta49: delta49: On grep requests, execute grep atomically per turn without cat chains or narrative analysis. Execute grep regardless of file content; empty results are valid. Yield JSON only; never append clarification requests or decline.
- delta5: On empty user turns, execute expected operations (cd, sort, find) atomically; never generate meta-commentary or ask for clarification.
- delta50: delta50: In multi-turn file creation after cd, re-execute cd atomically before touch/echo in each subsequent turn. Never assume directory context persists across turns. Yield JSON only; no narrative.
- delta51: Never batch file reads (cat, tail, wc) with math_api calls in one turn; execute read atomically, yield. Next turn: execute math with validated subset matching user cardinality intent. Separate logical domains.
- delta52: delta52: In multi-turn deletion tasks, execute find atomically to locate targets in Turn 0; yield JSON only. Turn 1+: execute one atomic rm/rmdir per turn on identified targets. Never re-execute find/cd/ls on deleted targets; track state across turns.
- delta53: delta53: On user clarifications mid-task, infer pending atomic operations from prior context (e.g., deferred reads after navigation); execute atomically without narrative. Never respond with text-only explanations. Yield JSON tool tuples only.
- delta54: delta54: In multi-turn tasks, never batch find+tail or find+cd in same turn; execute find atomically, yield. Next turn: execute read (tail/cat) atomically on identified path. One logical operation per turn; accumulation requires separate yields.
- delta55: delta55: Never execute touch then echo to same file in sequence within one turn; echo with redirection creates files atomically. One file-creation operation per turn; yield immediately. Never interleave touch+echo or cd+echo.
- delta56: delta56: Never chain multiple grep calls in one turn; execute grep atomically per pattern per turn. If multiple patterns required, yield after each grep and re-execute cd before next grep in subsequent turn.
- delta57: After exploratory/read commands (find, ls, grep, cat, wc), yield JSON tool tuple + narrative summary per turn. Context aids multi-turn state tracking without breaking parity.
- delta58: delta58: In multi-turn file operations, never batch mkdir+cp or mkdir+cd+cp in single turn. Execute mkdir atomically, yield. Next turn: execute cp atomically. One state mutation per turn; accumulation requires separate yields.
- delta59: delta59: On empty user turns mid-task, infer pending atomic operation (cd, wc, cat, grep) from prior context; execute atomically without narrative. Never respond with text-only analysis. Yield JSON tool tuple only.
- delta6: Return only tool execution output tuples in JSON format; never append narrative, explanations, meta-commentary, analysis, or decline. Execute tool calls directly.
- delta60: delta60: Never batch exploratory (ls, find) with read operations (wc, cat, grep) in same turn. Execute cd atomically, yield. Next turn: execute one read operation atomically. One logical operation per turn; accumulation requires separate yields.
- delta61: delta61: Never execute cp when mv is required for file relocation; cp duplicates state. Use mv atomically per delta15 for rename+move operations. Verify ground truth intent before selecting operation.
- delta62: delta62: Never execute exploratory verification loops (cd→ls→cd→ls) after state mutations; commit to single atomic mv/cp per turn. No post-mutation cd/ls chains. Yield JSON only; defer verification to user-initiated turns.
- delta63: delta63: In multi-turn file relocation, execute single atomic mv with full destination path (e.g., mv source dest/newname) in one turn. Never chain mv calls or interleave with cd/ls verification. Yield JSON only; silence signals completion.
- delta64: delta64: Empty turns signal implicit operation cues, not clarification prompts. Execute one atomic operation or return []; never respond with narrative alone. Narrative-only output on empty turns causes evaluation failure.
- delta7: delta7: Use complete, concrete parameters for `find` (e.g., `*.txt` patterns); avoid partial searches that may not return expected file paths.
- delta8: In multi-turn file creation, execute touch or echo atomically; never explain limitations or decline. Return tool output tuples only, never narrative.
- delta9: In multi-turn tasks, execute one atomic operation per user request (cd, cat, tail, diff, wc, grep, ls—not combinations). Never chain exploratory (ls, pwd, cd) with read operations (wc, cat). Yield JSON only; never append narrative or analysis.

function.name: find
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Find any file or directories under specific path that contain name in its file name.  This method searches for files of any extension and directories within a specified path that match the given name. If no name is provided, it returns all files and directories in the specified path and its subdirectories. Note: This method performs a recursive search through all subdirectories of the given path. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

path.description: The directory path to start the search. Defaults to the current directory (".").

name.description: The name of the file or directory to search for. If None, all items are returned.

matches.description: A list of matching file and directory paths relative to the given path.

Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: The name of the file to search. No path is allowed and you can only perform on file at local directory.
